records.text: The Bar of the State of Mayflower is hereby established as an administrative agency within the judicial branch of government. It shall operate under the supervision of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.

The Chief Justice may, at their discretion, designate an Associate Justice or another judicial officer to oversee and support the effective operation of the State Bar, ensuring it adheres to the provisions of this act and any relevant rules or regulations.
The State Bar shall have an official seal, which shall be reserved strictly for its official use and may not be used for any private purposes.
The State Bar shall have the legal capacity to sue and be sued under its own name.
This chapter may be cited as the "Judiciary Act."
For the purposes of this section:
(a) "State Bar" shall refer to the Bar of the State of Mayflower established under this act.
(b) "Supreme Court" shall refer to the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.
(c) "Active Member" shall refer to an attorney who is fully licensed and authorized to practice law in the State of Mayflower.
(d) "Provisional License" shall refer to a temporary license granted under this act.
(e) "Disciplinary Proceedings" shall refer to actions initiated to address allegations of professional misconduct or attorney incapacity.
The statutory officers of the State Bar shall include:
(a) The State Bar Director.
(b) The Chairman of the State Bar Ethics Committee.
(c) The Attorney General.
These officers shall be elected by a majority vote of all Associate Justices of the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.
If a vacancy arises unexpectedly, the Chief Justice may choose to appoint an interim Director(s) until a new election can be held.
The terms of the officers shall be determined by the Chief Justice.
The State Bar shall keep detailed financial records and prepare an annual budget if it decides to impose a levy for its operations. The budget shall be subject to the approval of the Supreme Court.

In accordance with the Chief Justice having oversight of the State Bar statutory to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1101.1, the Chief Justice shall be granted automatic membership on the State Bar. This shall take it's effectiveness after:
(a) The Chief Justice swear's his or her's oath
If a vacancy arises unexpectedly, the Chief Justice may choose to appoint an interim Director(s) until a new election can be held.
The terms of the officers shall be determined by the Chief Justice.
The State Bar shall keep detailed financial records and prepare an annual budget if it decides to impose a levy for its operations. The budget shall be subject to the approval of the Supreme Court.
The State Bar of the State of Mayflower shall have the delegated authority to examine, recommend and grant licensure to individuals seeking admission to practice law in this State.
The State Bar shall conduct all necessary evaluations, including the bar examination and character and fitness assessments, to determine an applicant’s qualifications.
No person shall be admitted to practice as an attorney or counselor in the State of Mayflower without fulfilling the requirements prescribed by the State Bar.
The State Bar shall retain ultimate and inherent authority over all matters concerning the admission to the practice of law in this State with the State Bar carrying out its functions.

The State Bar of the State of Mayflower is authorized to grant provisional licenses to individuals who meet specific criteria established by the Bar, allowing them to engage in limited legal practice under supervision for a defined period.
A provisional license may be granted for legitimate purposes, including but not limited to:
(a) Participation in a recognized degree course as established under 4 M.S.C. 4 § 1208(d).
(b) Participation in a recognized legal traineeship or apprenticeship program by a certified law firm;
(c) Temporary legal practice by out-of-state or foreign attorneys pending their full admission to the State Bar of Mayflower;
(d) Completion of practical training requirements mandated by the State Bar for full licensure.
Membership in the State Bar of Mayflower is divided into the following categories:
(a) Active Membership: Attorneys who are fully licensed and authorized to practice law.
(b) Inactive Membership: Attorneys not currently practicing law, who may be exempt from paying levies.

(c) Abeyance Membership: Attorneys whose membership is temporarily suspended due to disciplinary action, failure to meet obligations, or holding a position that places them under judicial trust. These members may not practice law until reinstated by the Bar.

(d) Provisional Membership: Attorneys holding a provisional license, allowing them to practice law under supervision. They must transition to active membership upon fulfilling all requirements for full licensure or when their provisional status expires.
The State Bar has the authority to adopt, implement, and enforce rules governing the practice of law and the conduct of its members.
The State Bar shall establish and maintain the Mayflower Rules of Professional Conduct, which outline the ethical and professional responsibilities of all attorneys licensed in this State.
In consultation of its committee members, the State Bar may also adopt additional rules, regulations and procedures necessary for:
(a) Disciplining, suspending, or disbarring attorneys who violate professional standards or commit acts of misconduct;
(b) Administering and enforcing legal education requirements to maintain attorney competency and ethical practice;
(c) Resolving disputes between attorneys and their clients, including fee arbitration.
(d) All rules adopted by the State Bar are binding on members upon adoption and must be made publicly available. The Bar may amend or repeal rules as necessary.
Before adopting, amending, or repealing any rule, the State Bar shall:
(a) Provide notice of the proposed rule to all members and the public, specifying changes and inviting written comments;
(b) Consult with members if deemed necessary;
(c) Submit the proposed rule to the Supreme Court for final approval before it takes effect.
(d) All rules become effective once enacted and must be published in a way that is accessible to all members and the public.
The State Bar shall develop and administer all bar examinations in a manner that ensures fairness, transparency, and equal access for all applicants.
The State Bar must provide applicants with adequate resources and information regarding the examination, including:
(a) Published guidelines;
(b) Subjects tested, and relevant rules; and
(c) Information on examination dates, deadlines and procedures.
The State Bar shall establish and publish a clear grade boundary or passing score for the examination.

The Supreme Court of Mayflower has exclusive jurisdiction over rules governing the admission to practice law. The Supreme Court holds sole authority to establish, amend, and enforce all standards and rules related to attorney admission.

The officers and directors of the State Bar of Mayflower do not have the authority to approve, disapprove, regulate, or administer any rule regarding admissions. All admissions standards, procedures, and requirements are prescribed and administered solely by the Supreme Court.

The State Bar has exclusive jurisdiction over rules governing the admission to practice law and holds sole authority to establish, amend, and enforce all standards and rules related to attorney admission. The State Bar’s role also includes executing the examination, character and fitness assessments, and other processes.
All attorneys admitted to practice law in the State of Mayflower are subject to the disciplinary and disability jurisdiction of the State Bar, including its committees.

The State Bar has the authority to investigate, adjudicate, and impose appropriate sanctions for violations of professional conduct or instances of attorney incapacity, following rules and procedures enacted.
The Supreme Court shall have the exclusive ability to appeal any investigations or actions taken as repritorive or as a strict punishment on any Attorney within the State Bar.
In any disciplinary or disability proceeding, the person involved shall be afforded due process, including a fair opportunity to present representations and defend against the allegations.
The person has the right to be notified of the charges, be represented by counsel, present evidence, and call and cross-examine witnesses as part of their defense.

Upon receiving credible information that an attorney’s continued practice poses a substantial threat to the public or the integrity of the legal profession, the State Bar or a delegated committee may suspend the attorney’s license pending further investigation.

An interim suspension under this Section may be imposed while the matter is under investigation. The subject shall be notified of the suspension without delay and afforded an opportunity to contest the suspension.

An interim suspension pursuant to this Section shall not exceed fourteen (14) calendar days from the date of issuance. The suspension shall terminate automatically upon the period of expiration, unless, prior to expiration, an extension is granted by an extraordinary order upon showing good cause that the continued suspension is necessary to protect the public, or the integrity of the legal profession.

The State Bar shall provide notice of the interim suspension to the subject within two (2) hours of its issuance, and shall be obligated to notify relevant judicial officers of such suspension to ensure affected clients are informed and provided adequate time to secure alternative counsel.

The State Bar, acting as a precepting authority under the direction of the Director, may impose and enforce a monthly levy payable by all attorneys registered to practice law in the State of Mayflower.
The amount of the levy and the payment schedule shall be determined by the State Bar, subject to the approval of the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.
A levy cannot be imposed or amended without the support of at least 2/3rds of the sitting Justices of the Supreme Court, and it may only be imposed on the “Active” class of membership.
The levy must be used strictly to fund the administration and operation of the State Bar, including:
(a) regulatory activities;
(b) member services;
(c) educational programs;
(d) public protection initiatives;
(e) pro bono programs to assist indigent populations;
(f) reappropriation of funds into the Administrative Office of the State of Mayflower Courts;
(g) failure to pay the levy as prescribed may result in penalties, including suspension of membership; and
(h) in cases of financial hardship, the Bar may choose to waive fees for members.

The Office of Public Defenders is hereby established as an administrative agency within the judicial branch of government. It shall operate under the supervision of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.

records.text: The Chief Justice may, at their discretion, designate an Associate Justice or another judicial officer to oversee and support the effective operation of the Office ensuring it adheres to the provisions of this act and any relevant rules or regulations.

context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office shall have an official seal, which shall be reserved strictly for its official use and may not be used for any private purposes.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office shall have the legal capacity to sue and be sued under its own name.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office of Public Defenders shall be governed by an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court who shall serve as the supervising authority of the Office. The Justice shall be responsible for ensuring that the Office operates effectively and in accordance with the provisions of this act.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Associate Justice, acting as supervisor, shall appoint a Chief Public Defender, who must be a member of the Mayflower State Bar, and shall manage the day-to-day operations of the Office, including the supervision of all public defenders and support staff.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Chief Public Defender shall serve a term determined by the supervising authority and may be reappointed at the discretion of the supervising authority.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office of Public Defenders shall provide legal representation to any individual who:

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (a) is charged with a criminal offense in the State of Mayflower and faces potential incarceration; and

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (b) is determined by the court to be financially unable to obtain private counsel.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office shall also provide representation in civil cases where such representation is mandated by law or necessary to protect a fundamental right, subject to available resources.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The scope of representation shall include all stages of criminal and civil proceedings, from initial appearance through trial, sentencing, appeal, and post-conviction relief.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office may elect to create specialized units for complex cases where it deems necessary.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office of Public Defenders shall recruit and employ qualified attorneys as public defenders to ensure that it meets its obligations under this act.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Chief Public Defender, in consultation with the Supervising Justice, shall be responsible for overseeing the recruitment, selection, and appointment of public defenders.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Be members in good standing of the Mayflower State Bar;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Demonstrate intention or experience in criminal defense or the specific areas of law relevant to their assigned duties; and

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Possess a strong commitment to public service and the protection of clients' constitutional rights.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Eligibility for representation by the Office of Public Defenders shall be determined based on financial guidelines established and approved by the Supreme Court of Mayflower.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.part: PART V. APPOINTMENT OF A PUBLIC DEFENDER

records.text: A person is considered indigent if their income and assets are insufficient to afford private legal representation, considering the complexity of the case and associated costs.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.part: PART V. APPOINTMENT OF A PUBLIC DEFENDER

records.text: The court shall make the determination of indigence, which shall be reviewed periodically and adjusted if the individual’s financial circumstances change.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.part: PART V. APPOINTMENT OF A PUBLIC DEFENDER

records.text: The Office of Public Defenders shall operate independently from political influence, with public defenders performing their duties free from external pressures and in strict adherence to professional ethics.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Public defenders shall adhere to the Mayflower Rules of Professional Conduct and any additional ethical guidelines set forth by the State Bar.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The payment and compensation of all Public Defenders shall be set as equal to the compensation of the average State Attorney.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Public defenders shall have the authority to make all decisions regarding representation, case strategy, and defense without interference from any external entity, including the Department of Justice, or the Attorney General and his respective officers, and sub-agents.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Chief Public Defender shall develop policies to ensure that caseloads are manageable and that public defenders can provide competent and diligent representation to each client.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office shall establish performance standards and regularly evaluate the effectiveness and quality of the legal representation provided by public defenders.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Office may elect to subcontract some of its legal services to a private law firm if such subcontracting is deemed necessary to ensure effective representation, manage caseloads, or address specialized legal needs.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Any subcontractor under section (c) of this Section must:

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (a) be in good standing with the Mayflower State Bar;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (b) demonstrate a history of providing high-quality legal services, with particular experience in criminal defense or the specific area of law for which they are being engaged; and

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (c) adhere to the same ethical and professional standards required of public defenders, including compliance with the Mayflower Rules of Professional Conduct.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The decision to subcontract services shall be made by the Chief Public Defender, in consultation with the Supervising Justice, and must be based on clear and documented criteria, including but not limited to:

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (a) the need to address caseload overflow or conflicts of interest;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (b) the specialized expertise required for complex cases; and

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (c) the availability of resources within the OPD to handle the case internally.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The subcontracting arrangement shall be subject to review to ensure compliance with this act and the delivery of high-quality legal services.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Any subcontracting must be provided with a notice under this section to the general public notifying them of such changes to services offered.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The subcontractor may not charge for any services from its client, but may receive appropriations from the Office if agreed upon.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Supervising Justice may, at their discretion, initiate the removal or dismissal of the Chief Public Defender if it is determined that such action is necessary for the effective operation of the Office of Public Defenders.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Grounds for removal may include, but are not limited to:

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (a) failure to perform duties effectively or competently;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (b) misconduct or breach of ethical obligations;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (c) inability to maintain the confidence and trust necessary for the proper functioning of the Office;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: (d) any other reason that, in the judgment of the Supervising Justice, warrants removal in the best interest of the Office and its clients.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: Before the Chief is removed or dismissed, the Supervising Justice must seek and obtain permission from the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Mayflower. Upon approval by the Chief Justice, the Supervising Justice shall have the authority to immediately remove the Chief from their position and appoint an interim Chief until a permanent replacement is selected. The Supervising Justice shall then initiate the process to appoint a new Chief Public Defender as provided under Sections of this act.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE

records.text: The Supreme Court may appoint a marshal, who shall be subject to removal by the Court, and may fix his compensation.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: The marshal may, with the approval of the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower, appoint and fix the compensation of necessary assistants and other employees to attend the Court, and necessary custodial employees under his supervison.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: There shall be a Supreme Court Police Division established within a department, as designated by the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower, with the approval of the Supreme Court of Mayflower and the Head of the relevant department that will house this division.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: The marshal shall:

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (a) attend the Court at its sessions;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (b) serve and execute all processes and orders issued by the Court or a member thereof;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (c) take charge of all property of the State of Mayflower used by the Court or its members;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (d) oversee the Supreme Court Police; and

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (e) perform any act and take any measure necessary and proper for the efficient performance of the duties with the approval of the Supreme Court.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: In accordance with regulations prescribed by the Marshal of the Supreme Court and approved by the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower, the Marshal and the Supreme Court Police shall have authority—

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (a) to police the Supreme Court Building and grounds and adjacent streets to protect individuals and property;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (b) in any location, to protect—

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (i) the Chief Justice, any Associate Justice of the Supreme Court, and any official guest of the Supreme Court;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (ii) any officer or employee of the Supreme Court while that officer or employee is performing official duties; and

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (iii) any member of the immediate family of the Chief Justice, any Associate Justice, or any officer of the Supreme Court if the Marshal determines such protection is necessary, or if directed by the Chief Justice.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (c) while performing duties necessary to carry out paragraph (1) or (2), to make arrests for any violation of State law and any regulation under State law; and

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (d) to carry firearms as may be required while performing duties under this subchapter, part III of this subchapter, and subchapter IV.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: Public travel in, and occupancy of, the Supreme Court grounds is restricted to the sidewalks and other paved surfaces.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: It is unlawful—

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (a) to offer or expose any article for sale in the Supreme Court Building or grounds;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (b) to display a sign, placard, or other form of advertisement in the Building or grounds; or

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: (c) to solicit fares, alms, subscriptions, or contributions in the Building or grounds.

context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: It is unlawful to discharge a firearm or explosive, set fire to a combustible, make a harangue or oration, or utter loud, threatening, or abusive language in the Supreme Court Building or grounds.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER III. MARSHAL AND THE SUPREME COURT POLICE

records.text: It is unlawful to parade, stand, or move in processions or assemblages in the Supreme Court Building or grounds, or to display in the Building and grounds a flag, banner, or device designed or adapted to bring into public notice a party, organization, or movement.

records.text: The Supreme Court and all inferior Courts may issue all writs necessary or appropriate in aid of their respective jurisdictions and agreeable to the usages and principles of law.
An alternative writ or rule may be issued by a justice or judge of a court that has jurisdiction.

A quo warranto may be issued from the Mayflower District Court for the judicial district in which the Capitol resides in the name of the State of Mayflower against a person who within the State of Mayflower usurps, intrudes into, or unlawfully holds or exercises, a franchise conferred by the State or a public office of the State of Mayflower, civil or military. The proceedings shall be deemed a civil action. No writ of quo warranto may be filed without the consent of the Attorney General.
The courts shall prescribe manner and method for the issuance of these writs.

A defendant in any criminal action has the right of appeal under the rules hereinafter prescribed, and provided, however, before the defendant who has been convicted upon either his plea of guilty or plea of nolo contendere before the court and the court, upon the election of the defendant, assesses punishment and the punishment does not exceed the punishment recommended by the prosecutor and agreed to by the defendant and his attorney may prosecute his appeal, he must have permission of the trial court, except on those matters which have been raised by written motion filed prior to trial.
The State is entitled to appeal an order of a court in a criminal case if the order:
(a) dismisses an indictment, information, or complaint or any portion of an indictment, information, or complaint;
(b) arrests or modifies a judgment;
(c) grants a new trial;
(d) sustains a claim of former jeopardy; or

(e) grants a motion to suppress evidence, a confession, or an admission, if jeopardy has not attached in the case and if the prosecuting attorney certifies to the trial court that the appeal is not taken for the purpose of delay and that the evidence, confession, or admission is of substantial importance in the case.
The State is entitled to a stay in the proceedings pending the disposition of an appeal under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1401.2.
At any time, over any arrest, a person may petition the District Court for a writ of habeas corpus.
(a) The fact that a person was released from prison shall not hold bar or make moot any petition therein.
(b) The writ shall be directed to the person who has made the arrest, furthermore they shall also serve as the respondent to which a petition shall be served onto.
(c) The State shall serve as counsel for the respondent.
(i) The State may refuse to defend the respondent in a matter of a Habeas Corpus petition, if the State issues an order vacating the arrest which was the basis of the petition filed.
(d) Every provision relating to the writ of habeas corpus shall be most favorably construed in order to give effect to the remedy, and protect the rights of the person seeking relief under it.
(e) Notwithstanding any other law, a clerk of a court may not require a filing fee from an individual who files an application or petition for a writ of habeas corpus.
The following are the only authorized remedies:
(a) immediate release from prison or detainment if timely sought; and
(b) expungement of record.
The Supreme Court may promulgate rules pursuant to this statute.

The District Court may render a declaratory judgment having the effect of a final judgment as to the rights and other legal relations of the parties to a justiciable controversy whether or not further relief is or could be claimed. If the court declines to render such a judgment it shall state its grounds. Any such declaration shall have the force and effect of a final judgment or decree and shall be reviewable as such.

The common law and statutes of Pax Britannia, of a general and not local nature, as they existed on the 4th Day of July, 1776, are hereby declared to be in force in this state, except as otherwise provided. Such laws shall remain in effect unless they are inconsistent with the Constitution and laws of the Union of Columbia or the acts of the state legislature.
All expungements are to be titled "Ex parte [name]," and take place as a proceeding against the Department of Justice.

(a) Unless the Attorney General or his designee appears to argue against expunction after notice being provided to the Attorney General of the filing of such expunction, the expungement petition will continue to be heard ex parte.

(i) In lieu of appearing, the Attorney General or his designee may submit a statement in support or in opposition to the expungement petition, which will be enetered into the court record for consideration of the assigned judge.

(b) If the Attorney General or his designee appears, they shall argue for the interests of the State in regard to the expunction. The expungement petition shall instead be titled "[Name of Petitioner] v. State of Mayflower."

records.text: A judge, upon the sentencing phase of a criminal case, shall set a period where a person must wait to expunge their conviction. Such a period shall be no longer than 8 months.
If no minimum period is specified explicitly, then a person must wait at least 4 months before expunging their conviction.
A conviction may be expunged before the preset time upon consent of the government.
Further requirements for a conviction expungement are
(a) no criminal record of arrest within the past six (6) months;
(b) letter of apology with true remorse issued both to the people of the State and to the victims;
(c) a Plan to proceed forward without engaging in criminal conduct; and
(d) a public hearing with the government present.

The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or a designated Associate Justice, is authorized to assign any Supreme Court Justice to temporarily sit as a judge in a lower court, including the district courts.

The Chief Judge of a county shall submit a written notice to the Supreme Court of Mayflower for temporary assignments to the lower court to alleviate a backlog of cases and to provide additional judicial resources in regions experiencing high caseloads.
The Chief Justice, in consultation with the Associate Justices, will review and approve or deny requests for temporary assignments.

These assignments shall only be temporary and the duration is to be determined on a case-by-case basis. If there is a substantial need for aid from the Supreme Court, then the assignment duration may be extended.

Justices who sit as judges in a lower court shall have the full judicial authority of the lower court to which they are assigned, including the power to hear cases, issue rulings, and manage court procedures.
The Supreme Court Justice shall operate within the jurisdiction of the lower court, adhering to applicable procedural and substantive laws.
A Supreme Court Justice who has presided over a case during a temporary assignment in a lower court shall recuse themselves from hearing that case at the appellate level.

records.text: A search warrant is an order in writing, in the name of the people, signed by a justice, judge, or magistrate, directed to a peace officer, commanding him or her to search for a person or persons, a thing or things, or personal property, and, in the case of a thing or things or personal property, bring the same before the magistrate.
A search warrant may be issued upon any of the following grounds:
(a) When the property was stolen or embezzled.
(b) When the property or things were used as the means of committing a felony.

(c) When the property or things are in the possession of any person with the intent to use them as a means of committing a public offense, or in the possession of another to whom he or she may have delivered them for the purpose of concealing them or preventing them from being discovered.

(d) When the property or things to be seized consist of any item or constitute any evidence that tends to show a felony has been committed, or tends to show that a particular person has committed a felony.
(e) When there is a warrant to arrest a person.

(f) When the property or things to be seized include a firearm or any other deadly weapon at the scene of, or at the premises occupied or under the control of the person arrested in connection with, a domestic violence incident involving a threat to human life or a physical assault.
(g) When the item or substance to be seized is unlawfully possessed or stored in any vehicle, domicile, or storage unit.
The property, things, person, or persons described in part I may be taken on the warrant from any place, or from any person in whose possession the property or things may be.

Notwithstanding other provisions, arrest warrants may only be applied for during cases in which exigent circumstances exist and the person has left the immediate presence of law enforcement officers [LTAA] who have probable cause to effectuate an arrest.
Arrest warrants may also be issued to a Defendant in a criminal matter, upon acceptance of the Indictment or Information with probable cause found to proceed, and:
(a) The charges are felony in nature, or;
(b) Good cause is established by an attorney for the government on how the Defendant poses a risk to public safety.
Upon the warrant’s execution, the documents and records shall be made open to the public as a judicial record in a timely manner.
A search warrant may be made returnable before the issuing magistrate or his court.
No warrant shall be issued by a justice, judge, or magistrate where they are employed by the same law enforcement agency that filed for the warrant.
Unless otherwise deemed necessary by a judge, warrants shall be executed by the county law enforcement agency of the political subdivision in which the warrant was issued, except under the following:

(a) Any search warrant request that is submitted by an employee of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation as a result of affidavits filed by the bureau, or cases prosecuted by the Department of Justice, shall fall under the jurisdiction of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation and shall be directed as such for execution.

(b) Any search warrant that was submitted which involves goods and items relating to military-grade equipment, the Mayflower National Guard, Military Police shall have jurisdiction over its execution and shall be directed as such for execution.

(c) Any search warrant request that is submitted by an employee of the State Bureau of Investigations (SBI) as a result of affidavits filed by the SBI shall fall under the jurisdiction of the Mayflower State Police and shall be directed as such for execution.
(i) For the purposes of this section, the term “State Bureau of Investigations” shall be defined as: the division under the Mayflower State Police entitled the "State Bureau of Investigations."

(d) MILITARY ARREST ORDERS. Any arrest warrant or military arrest order issued pursuant to this Title which involves members of the Mayflower National Guard, their property, or matters under the jurisdiction of the Military Police thereof, shall be executed by the Mayflower National Guard Military Police.

When the officer takes property under the warrant, he must give a receipt for the property taken (specifying it in detail) to the person from whom it was taken by him, or in whose possession it was found; or, in the absence of any person, he must leave it in the place where he found the property.
For the purposes of this Chapter, the term "political subdivision" shall have the same meaning as the definition adopted in Article III of the Constitution.

records.text: No individual may be appointed as a magistrate unless they have been a member in good standing of the bar of the State of Mayflower for at least two (2) months.

The term of a full time magistrate shall be three (3) months. Upon the expiration of their term, a magistrate may continue to perform duties until a successor is appointed, or fifteen (15) days, whichever is shorter.

A magistrate may be removed from office during their term solely on the grounds of incompetence, misconduct, neglect of duty, or physical or mental incapacity. Such removal shall require the concurrence of a majority of the appointing judges. The magistrate shall be provided with a detailed specification of the charges and afforded an opportunity to respond to the charges before any final decision is made.
Magistrates may not hold any civil office under the State of Mayflower unless specifically approved by the Judicial Conference.
Magistrates are permitted to practice law in private or on behalf of the government.
A candidate for magistrate may be appointed by the Governor, subject to the advice and consent of the Senate.

Each magistrate appointed under this section shall have authority within the district where the appointing court holds sessions, at any other locations where that court may operate, and in any other areas as permitted by law, to:
(a) issue search warrants and arrest warrants upon a competent finding of probable cause;
(b) conduct hearings and trials, both for civil cases and criminal;
(c) hear evidence;
(d) compel production of relevant evidence, including books, papers, vouchers, documents, and other writings;
(e) rule on admissibility of evidence;
(f) issue summons and attachments for the appearance of witnesses;
(g) examine witnesses;
(h) swear witnesses for hearings and trials;
(i) perform any act and take any measure necessary and proper for the efficient performance of the duties assigned by the district court judge; and
(j) any or other power conferred or imposed upon Magistrates by any other law.
(a) motions for injunctive relief;
(b) motion for judgment on the pleadings;
(c) motions for summary judgment;
(d) motion to dismiss or quash an indictment or information made by the defendant;
(e) motion to suppress evidence;
(f) motion to dismiss;
(g) maintain a class action;
(h) motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim upon which relief may be granted; and
(i) motions for involuntary dismissal of an action.
A judge may reconsider any pretrial matter determined by a magistrate under this section where it is demonstrated that the magistrate’s decision is clearly erroneous or contrary to law.

A judge may, by order, designate a magistrate to conduct hearings, including evidentiary hearings, and to submit to the judge proposed findings of fact and recommendations for the disposition of any matter excepted under this section.

At the conclusion of any hearing conducted under this section, the magistrate shall transmit to the judge all papers and documents relating to the case, including the magistrate's findings of fact and recommendations;
a statement confirming that notice of the findings and recommendations, along with the right to request a hearing before the judge, has been duly given to all parties.
The magistrate shall file with the court any proposed findings and recommendations made under this section, and shall cause a copy thereof to be served upon all parties forthwith.

The judge shall adopt, modify, or reject the magistrate's recommendations no later than the fifth working day after the date the judge receives the recommendations. If the judge does not take action within the time provided by this subsection, the recommendations of the magistrate shall be deemed adopted by the judge.
Any party may, within fourteen (14) days of being served with a copy of the proposed findings and recommendations, file written objections thereto in accordance with the rules of court.

Upon consideration of any objections duly filed under this section, a judge shall make a de novo determination of the matters objected to, and may accept, reject, or modify, in whole or in part, the findings or recommendations made by the magistrate, receive further evidence, or remit the matter to the magistrate with directions.
A magistrate shall not be permitted or assigned to any category of cases that include:
(a) questions of vast economic and political significance;
(b) cases in which the state is seeking imposition of capital punishment; or
(c) cases that involve a significant and complex constitutional issue.
A magistrate appointed under this act shall, within the jurisdiction prescribed by their appointment, possess the authority to exercise contempt powers as set out in this section.

A magistrate shall have the authority to summarily punish, by fine or imprisonment, or both, any contempt committed in their presence that constitutes misbehavior obstructing the administration of justice for no more than . Such an order of contempt shall be issued in accordance with the applicable rules of criminal procedure.

In any case where a magistrate presides with the consent of the parties, or in any misdemeanor case proceeding before a magistrate, the magistrate shall have the authority to punish criminal contempt involving disobedience or resistance to the magistrate’s lawful writ, process, order, rule, decree, or command, by fine or imprisonment, or both. Such contempt proceedings shall be conducted with appropriate notice and hearing, as provided by the rules of criminal procedure.

Appeals of a magistrate’s contempt order under this Clause shall be directed to the appropriate appellate court in cases proceeding with the consent of the parties, or to the higher court in other cases

A magistrate’s order imposing imprisonment for contempt shall not exceed twenty (20) minutes in total unless a District Court Judge co-signs the order. Any contempt order resulting in imprisonment beyond twenty (20) minutes shall be presented to a judge for review and co-signature.
No fine imposed by a magistrate for contempt shall exceed the amount of three hundred (300) dollars.
The assigned judge on a case may revoke a Magistrate's order to hold a subject in contempt if there is a good reason and cause at any time.

records.text: Cases in the Supreme Court may be reviewed by the Supreme Court through the following means, but not limited to:
(a) By writ of certiorari, which may be granted upon the petition of any party involved in a civil or criminal case, whether before or after the judgment or decree has been rendered;

(b) By certification from any court, at any time, of any question of law arising in a civil or criminal case on which the court seeks guidance. Upon such certification, the Supreme Court may issue binding instructions or may direct that the entire record of the case be transmitted for consideration.

Any individual who intentionally and voluntarily caused the reasonable apprehension of an immediate harmful or offensive contact to another individual shall be liable for assault and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred thousand (200,000) dollars.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.part: PART I. TORTS AGAINST THE PERSON

records.text: Any individual who brought about an unconsented harmful or offensive contact with a person or to something closely associated with that person shall be liable for battery and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred thirty thousand (230,000) dollars.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.part: PART I. TORTS AGAINST THE PERSON

records.text: Any individual who, without legal authority or justification, restrains or restricts a person's movement within an area, or restrains the person’s permission is false imprisonment and shall be liable for punitive damages up to three hundred thousand (300,000) dollars.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.part: PART I. TORTS AGAINST THE PERSON

records.text: Any individual or entity whose negligence, wrongful act, or breach of duty results in the death of another person without that person’s consent, shall be liable for wrongful death and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one million (1,000,000) dollars.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.part: PART I. TORTS AGAINST THE PERSON

records.text: Every person who, under color of any statute, ordinance, regulation, custom, or usage, subjects, or causes to be subjected, any citizen of the State of Mayflower or other person within the jurisdiction thereof to the deprivation of any rights, privileges, or immunities secured by the Constitution and laws, shall be liable for deprivation of rights to the party injured in an action at law, suit in equity, or other proper proceeding for redress, except that in any action brought against a judicial officer for an act or omission taken in such officer’s judicial capacity, injunctive relief shall not be granted unless a declaratory decree was violated or declaratory relief was unavailable.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.part: PART I. TORTS AGAINST THE PERSON

records.text: If two or more persons conspire, for the purpose of depriving, either directly or indirectly, any person or class of persons of the equal protection of the laws, or of equal privileges and immunities under the laws; or for the purpose of preventing or hindering the constituted authorities of the State of Mayflower or its political subdivisions from giving or securing to all persons within the State the equal protection of the laws; in any case of conspiracy set forth in this section, if one or more persons engaged therein do, or cause to be done, any act in furtherance of the object of such conspiracy, whereby another is injured in his person or property, or deprived of having and exercising any right or privilege, the party so injured or deprived may have an action for the recovery of damages occasioned by such injury or deprivation, against any one or more of the conspirators.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.part: PART I. TORTS AGAINST THE PERSON

records.text: If two or more persons conspire to deter, by force, intimidation, or threat, any party or witness in any court of the State of Mayflower or its political subdivisions from attending such court, or from testifying to any matter pending therein, freely, fully, and truthfully, or to injure such party or witness in their person or property on account of their having so attended or testified; or if two or more persons conspire for the purpose of impeding, hindering, obstructing, or defeating, in any manner, the due course of justice in the State of Mayflower or its political subdivisions, with intent to deny to any citizen the equal protection of the laws, or to injure them or their property for lawfully enforcing, or attempting to enforce, the right of any person, or class of persons, to the equal protection of the laws, they shall be liable for civil conspiracy to obstruct justice and for damages arising therefrom.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.part: PART I. TORTS AGAINST THE PERSON

records.text: Any individual who fails to exercise the degree of care that a reasonably prudent person would under similar circumstances, resulting in harm to another individual, shall be liable for negligence and shall be liable for punitive damages up to five hundred thousand (500,000) dollars.

Any individual who violates a statute or regulation designed to protect a specific class of individuals from harm, and whose violation directly causes injury to another individual, shall be liable for negligence per se and shall be liable for punitive damages up to six hundred seventy five thousand (675,000) dollars.

Any individual who fails to perform a contractual obligation as agreed, without lawful excuse, and causes harm to the other party, shall be liable for breach of contract and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred fifty thousand (150,000) dollars.

Any employer who fails to exercise the degree of care that a reasonably prudent employer would under similar circumstances in hiring an employee, resulting in harm caused by the employee to another individual, shall be liable for negligent hiring and shall be liable for punitive damages up to four hundred thousand (400,000) dollars.

Any individual who intentionally enters the land of another without lawful excuse shall be liable for trespass to land and shall be liable for punitive damages up to seventy five thousand (75,000) dollars.

Any individual who intentionally interferes with the personal property of another shall be liable for trespass to chattels and shall be liable for punitive damages up to fifty thousand (50,000) dollars.

Any individual who intentionally interferes with the property of another with the intent to deprive the owner of the property shall be liable for conversion and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred thousand (100,000) dollars.

Any individual or organization that spreads a false and unprivileged publication by writing, printing, picture, effigy, or other fixed representation to the eye, which exposes any person to hatred, contempt, ridicule, or obloquy, or which causes him to be shunned or avoided, or which has a tendency to injure him in his occupation shall be liable for libel and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred fifty thousand (150,000) dollars.

Any individual who orally utters a false and unprivileged publication that exposes a person to hatred, contempt, or ridicule or which injures their reputation shall be liable for slander and shall be liable for punitive damages up to seventy five thousand (75,000) dollars.

Any individual who uses a legal process for an ulterior purpose, with the intention of achieving a result not intended by the process, shall be liable for abuse of process and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred thousand (200,000) dollars.

Any individual who initiates a legal proceeding without probable cause, with malice or intent to harm, and the proceeding terminates in favor of the accused, shall be liable for malicious prosecution and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) dollars.

It shall be unlawful for any governmental authority, or any agent thereof, or any person acting on behalf of a governmental authority, to engage in a pattern or practice of conduct by law enforcement officers that deprives persons of rights, privileges, or immunities secured or protected by the Constitution or laws of the State of Mayflower or Union of Columbia.

(a) Whenever the Attorney General has reasonable cause to believe that a violation of 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.5 has occurred, the Attorney General, for or in the name of the State of Mayflower, may in a civil action obtain appropriate equitable and declaratory relief to eliminate the pattern or practice.

Any individual who is a public servant and commits an act relating to his office but constitutes an unauthorized exercise of his official functions, where a reasonable person with his training, expertise, and experiences should know that such act is unauthorized; or refrains from performing a duty which is imposed upon him by law or is clearly inherent in the nature of his office.
(a) The plaintiff must prove that the official misconduct from that individual caused injury to himself, and that the plaintiff is entitled to relief from the courts.

(b) Any individual who is a public servant and commits the aforementioned shall be liable for compensatory damages; injunctive reliefs restraining the individual from performing a certain action, or orders instructing the individual to perform a certain action; and punitive damages up to $75,000

(c) Such suits shall proceed in a form of quasi-official capacity, such that the defendants shall be named as parties in official capacity; however if the courts or an arbitrator wish to provide monetary damages to the plaintiff, then it shall be the duty of the defendant’s individual capacity to pay such damages as ordered.

Any individual who willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows, harasses, or engages in a pattern of conduct directed at another individual that would cause a reasonable person to feel fear for their own safety shall be liable for the tort of stalking and may be subject to punitive damages up to two hundred and fifty thousand (250,000) dollars.
(a) The individual aggrieved by such conduct may seek relief in the form of an injunction or declaratory judgment.

(b) Upon a verified petition and showing of conduct that would support a claim under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.7, a court may issue a temporary injunction for protection against stalking, effective for no more than fourteen (14) days provided the petition establishes that the respondent’s conduct would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety; such an order may be granted without notice to the other party. An injunction may be extended until final judgment only upon a showing of irreparable harm, or a substantial threat thereof, to the petitioner; such an order may only be granted with notice to the other party. A party must first initiate a claim under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.7 to petition for an injunction under this subsection.

Any individual who publicly discloses information about another that places the individual in a false light, and where the false light would be highly offensive to a reasonable person and was made with knowledge of or reckless disregard for its falsity, shall be liable for false light invasion of privacy and punitive damages up to fifty thousand (50,000) dollars.

Any individual who knowingly makes a false representation with the intent to deceive another, and where such representation is reasonably relied upon and causes actual harm, shall be liable for fraud. The injured party may recover compensatory damages and, where appropriate, punitive damages up to seven hundred fifty thousand dollars (750,000).

Any individual who intentionally interferes with a contractual or business relationship between other parties, causing harm to one of the parties, shall be liable for tortious interference and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred seventy five (175,000) dollars.

Any individual who enters into an agreement with two or more parties to deprive a third party of legal rights or to deceive a third party in order to achieve an illegal objective, resulting in harm to the third party, shall be liable for civil conspiracy and shall be liable for punitive damages up to three hundred thousand (300,000) dollars.

Any individual who knowingly discloses or misappropriates confidential business information or trade secrets without authorization and with the intent to gain an unfair competitive advantage shall be liable for misappropriation of trade secrets and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) dollars.

Any individual who, with intent to obtain money, property, services, or other benefit, knowingly threatens to expose, accuse, disgrace, or otherwise harm another unless such benefit is provided, and whose threat causes harm or coerced compliance, shall be liable for civil extortion and punitive damages up to three hundred seventy fifty thousand (375,000) dollars.

Any individual who, in breach of a fiduciary duty, acts contrary to the interests of the beneficiary by engaging in self-dealing, nondisclosure, or other disloyal conduct resulting in harm, shall be liable for breach of fiduciary duty and subject to compensatory and punitive damages up to five hundred thousand dollars (500,000).

In all cases of tortious conduct, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to seek remedies that include but are not limited to, compensatory damages, punitive damages, injunctive relief, and any other relief deemed appropriate by the court. The availability of remedies for each tort is not exclusive or limiting, and the non-exclusion of any particular remedy does not preclude its application or availability in any specific case.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.part: PART VI. REMEDIES BABY DOLPHIN PRICE

records.text: (a) Where the court finds that the tortious conduct was willful, malicious, reckless, or part of a pattern of repeated misconduct, it may, in the interest of justice, award punitive damages in excess of any statutory cap otherwise imposed by this title.
