context.part: PART VI. REMEDIES BABY DOLPHIN PRICE

records.text: As used in this act, the term “state agency” includes the executive departments, the judicial and legislative branches, the military departments, independent establishments of the State of Mayflower, and corporations primarily acting as instrumentalities or agencies of the State of Mayflower, but does not include any contractor with the State of Mayflower.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: “Employee of the government” includes (1) officers or employees of any state agency, members of the National Guard while engaged in training or duty, and persons acting on behalf of a state agency in an official capacity, temporarily or permanently in the service of the state, whether with or without compensation, and (2) any officer or employee of a state public defender organization, except when such officer or employee performs professional services in the course of providing representation.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: “Acting within the scope of his office or employment,” in the case of a member of the National Guard means acting in line of duty.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: The government shall be immune from all claims except those in this subchapter, and later laws in which liability is explicitly created against the government.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: No monetary damage shall be awarded in a case against the government, cases where the government is a party, or cases where the government has intervened, unless the government has consented to it through a statutory waiver.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: The Solicitor General may accept settlements on behalf of the government and issue orders or decrees in line with those settlements such that they are within the bounds of the law, charter, and constitution.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: The Solicitor General may intervene with the government as a defendant in cases against one’s individual capacity if they were in fact serving in an official capacity - or the government has a substantial interest in the outcome of the suit.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: The Solicitor General may refuse to defend an agent of the government if they were clearly acting in an individual capacity, or in a capacity that is not in line with the laws, directives, orders, policies, or standard operating procedures of the government and its agencies.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: Qualified immunity shall not be a valid affirmative defense if the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: If the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government, and the torts are alleged under this section, then the Solicitor General shall provide the relief as requested within the bounds of the law, charter, and constitution.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: The courts shall dismiss with prejudice all claims in which the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent, and that the Solicitor General provides relief as requested within the law, charter, and constitution.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: If the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government, then that agent shall be liable for the equitable offenses in his individual capacity, and the government shall cease to be a party and have interest in the case.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART II. GOVERNMENT IMMUNITY AND SOLICITOR GENERAL OVERSIGHT

records.text: Any individual seeking compensation for damages or other forms of relief, declaratory, injunctive, or otherwise, arising from tortious acts authorized by this section against the state, county, or municipal agencies and employees of the State and any political or administrative subdivision thereof must submit their claim to the Department of Justice. The claim should include detailed information about the nature of the tort, the alleged wrongful conduct, and the damages sought. The Attorney General shall prescribe regulations that detail additional elements that must be included in a claim.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: Upon receipt of the claim, the Department of Justice shall have a set period of seven (7) days to:

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: (a) accept the claim and propose a settlement;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: (b) deny the claim;

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: (c) request for more information; or

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: (d) open mediation between both parties to negotiate a resolution.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: If the Department of Justice chooses to deny the claim, then it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: If the Department of Justice chooses to request for more information, the claimant must respond within seven (7) days. If the claimant does so within this window, then the Department of Justice shall receive five (5) more days to process the claim. If the Department of Justice does not enter any action on the claim within this window, then it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act, similar to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.2(b). If the claimant does not provide the Department of Justice with the requested information within this window, then the Department of Justice shall not be required to review the claim any further and it shall be construed as if the claim was never sent to the Department of Justice.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: If the Department of Justice chooses to open arbitration, it must end within ten days of its initiation. In the event that it does not end within ten days, it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act, similar to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.2(b).

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: An individual must file a claim within three months from the date the claim accrued. Failure to file the claim within this specified period will result in the claim being barred and therefore not actionable in a State court.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: An action shall not be instituted upon a claim against the State of Mayflower, or any political or administrative subdivision thereof for relief for injury or loss of property or personal injury or death caused by the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the Government while acting within the scope of his office or employment, unless the claimant shall have first presented the claim to the Department of Justice and his claim shall have been finally denied by the agency in writing. The failure of the Department of Justice to make final disposition of a claim within one (1) month after it is filed shall, at the option of the claimant at any time thereafter, be deemed a final denial of the claim for purposes of this section.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART IV. DISPOSITION BY THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE AS A PREREQUISITE; EVIDENCE

records.text: Action under this section shall not be instituted for any sum in excess of the amount of the claim presented to the Department of Justice, except where the increased amount is based upon newly discovered evidence not reasonably discoverable at the time of presenting the claim to the Department of Justice, or upon allegation and proof of intervening facts, relating to the amount of the claim.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART IV. DISPOSITION BY THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE AS A PREREQUISITE; EVIDENCE

records.text: Disposition of any claim by the Attorney General or his designee shall not be competent evidence of liability or amount of damages.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART IV. DISPOSITION BY THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE AS A PREREQUISITE; EVIDENCE

records.text: The Attorney General or his designee, may consider, ascertain, adjust, determine, compromise, and settle any claim for money damages against the State of Mayflower for injury or loss of property or personal injury or death caused by the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the agency while acting within the scope of his office or employment, under circumstances where the State of Mayflower, if a private person, would be liable to the claimant in accordance with the law of the place where the act or omission occurred.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART V. ADMINISTRATIVE ADJUSTMENT OF CLAIMS

records.text: Subject to the provisions of this title relating to civil actions on tort claims against the State of Mayflower, any such award, compromise, settlement, or determination shall be final and conclusive on all officers of the Government, except when procured by means of fraud.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART V. ADMINISTRATIVE ADJUSTMENT OF CLAIMS

records.text: The acceptance by the claimant of any such award, compromise, or settlement shall be final and conclusive on the claimant, and shall constitute a complete release of any claim against the State of Mayflower and against the employee of the government whose act or omission gave rise to the claim, by reason of the same subject matter.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART V. ADMINISTRATIVE ADJUSTMENT OF CLAIMS

records.text: The Attorney General or his designee, shall report semiannually to the Legislature all claims paid by it under 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3204.1-3204.3, stating the name of each claimant, the amount claimed, the amount awarded, and a brief description of the claim.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: The State of Mayflower shall be liable, respecting the provisions of this title relating to tort claims, in the same manner and to the same extent as a private individual under like circumstances, but shall not be liable for interest prior to judgment or for punitive damages.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART VII. LIABILITY OF THE STATE OF MAYFLOWER

records.text: If, however, in any case wherein death was caused, the State of Mayflower shall be liable for actual or compensatory damages, measured by the pecuniary injuries resulting from such death to the persons respectively.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART VII. LIABILITY OF THE STATE OF MAYFLOWER

records.text: With respect to any claim under this chapter, the State of Mayflower shall be entitled to assert any defense based upon judicial or legislative immunity which otherwise would have been available to the employee of the State of Mayflower whose act or omission gave rise to the claim, as well as any other defenses to which the State of Mayflower is entitled.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART VII. LIABILITY OF THE STATE OF MAYFLOWER

records.text: The Attorney General or his designee may arbitrate, compromise, or settle any claim initiated, after the commencement of an action thereon.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: The remedy against the State of Mayflower provided by this act for injury or loss of property, or personal injury or death arising or resulting from the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the Government while acting within the scope of his office or employment is exclusive of any other civil action or proceeding for money damages by reason of the same subject matter against the employee whose act or omission gave rise to the claim. Any other civil action or proceeding for money damages arising out of or relating to the same subject matter against the employee is precluded without regard to when the act or omission occurred.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: The previous paragraph does not extend or apply to a civil action against an employee of the Government—

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: (a) which is brought for a violation of the Constitution of the State of Mayflower, or

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: (b) which is brought for a violation of a statute of the State of Mayflower under which such action against an individual is otherwise authorized.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: The Solicitor General shall defend any civil action or proceeding brought in any court against any employee of the Government for any such damage or injury.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: The Solicitor General shall certify whether the defendant employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment at the time of the incident out of which the claim arose.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: Upon certification by the Solicitor General that the defendant employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment at the time of the incident out of which the claim arose, any civil action or proceeding commenced upon such claim in a Mayflower district court shall be deemed an action against the State of Mayflower under the provisions of this title and all references thereto, and the State of Mayflower shall be substituted as the party defendant.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: In the event that the Solicitor General has refused to certify scope of office or employment under this section, the employee may at any time before trial petition the court to find and certify that the employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment. Upon such certification by the court, such action or proceeding shall be deemed to be an action or proceeding brought against the State of Mayflower under the provisions of this title and all references thereto, and the State of Mayflower shall be substituted as the party defendant.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: Whenever an action or proceeding in which the State of Mayflower is substituted as the party defendant under this subsection is dismissed for failure first to present a claim pursuant to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3204.1, such a claim shall be deemed to be timely presented under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3209.2 if—

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: (a) the claim would have been timely had it been filed on the date the underlying civil action was commenced, and

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: (b) the claim is presented to the Department of Justice within fifteen days after dismissal of the civil action.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE

records.text: Every civil action commenced against the State of Mayflower shall be barred unless the complaint is filed within three months after the right of action first accrues.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:
context.chapter: CHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. CLAIMS AGAINST THE STATE
context.part: PART X. TIME FOR COMMENCING ACTION AGAINST THE STATE OF MAYFLOWER

records.text: A tort claim against the State of Mayflower shall be forever barred unless it is presented in writing to the Department of Justice within three months after such claim accrues.

records.text: The term “physician” shall refer to:
(a) Any member employed or appointed to the State Medical Examiner’s Office as a medical doctor.
(b) Any employee of a fire department, selected by their department head, with the necessary qualifications prescribed in standards written by the respective fire department.

This chapter may be cited as the "Capital Punishment Act."
“Capital punishment” or “death penalty” shall be defined as the judgment of death upon an individual convicted of a crime described in this act as a “capital felony”.

A “capital felony” shall refer to any of the following crimes listed in this subsection that shall be punishable by death upon the court deeming such sentence appropriate, unless otherwise provided further by law:
(a) 1 M.S.C. § 1105 "Treason."
(b) 1 M.S.C. § 1104 "Criminal Anarchy."
(c) 1 M.S.C. § 1102 "Espionage."
(d) 1 M.S.C. § 2101 "First-degree murder."

A “death warrant” shall refer to the issuance of a warrant by the court upon a judgment of death ordering for the search and seizure of all property, seizure of all properties leased, burning of any vehicles, aircrafts or boats owned, seizure of all money, and revocation of all certifications held from the individual imposed, as well as capital punishment to be executed at a specific date prescribed by the court.
A person, upon whom has been imposed the judgment of death, shall be transferred to the custody and care of the Attorney General through the Mayflower State Police.
A death warrant shall be signed by the Court upon a judgment of death.
(a) A death warrant shall allow the search and seizure of all property stored within vehicles or residences unless otherwise prescribed.

A death warrant shall allow the search and seizure of all property stored within vehicles or residences, the seizure of all properties leased, burning of all vehicles, aircrafts, or boats owned, seizure of all money, and revocation of all certifications held from the individual imposed.
Upon the completion of the death warrant seizure and the issuance of a warrant receipt to the court. The court shall issue the maximum sentence time allowed by law within the in-game interface.
(a) If there is no maximum sentence limit, then the court shall issue a jail sentence of no more than 3 days, and no less than 1 day.
The judgment of death shall be executed either at the Mayflower State Detention Complex, or at any Mayflower National Guard base confined within a military exclusion zone.
(a) The Mayflower National Guard may not inhibit the movement or access of civilian law enforcement, prescribed witnesses, or attorneys present for the purposes of the execution.
The punishment of death shall be carried out by firing squad.

(a) Four (4) Troopers from the Mayflower State Police shall be appointed to serve as members of the firing squad, with one (1) Trooper at the rank of Sergeant or above serving as leader of the firing squad.

(b) If selected officers from either the Mayflower State Police are unavailable, The Department of Justice may request the use of other law enforcement officials from municipal or county political subdivision(s) to meet the requirement listed in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4306(a).
The Department of Justice shall develop rules and standards for the method and process of execution that do not violate the person’s constitutional rights.

A physician may attend an execution for the purpose of pronouncing death and may provide advice to officials for the purpose of developing an execution protocol to minimize the risk of pain to the inmate.
(a) The presence of a physician is not required unless prescribed by standards written by the Department of Justice or by mandate of the court.
(b) The physician, upon completion of the execution will prescribe and record the time of death of the inmate to be presented in the death warrant and returned to the court.
(c) If there is no physician present, the ranking official of the Justice Department present during the execution will record the time of death.
The Department of Justice may allow witnesses to be present during the execution;
(a) No more than ten (10) members may be present, not including officials carrying out the punishment.
(b) No person shall be a witness to an execution unless they are a resident of the State of Mayflower.
(c) At the request of the inmate, spiritual members or ministers of the gospel shall be permitted to be present at the execution not exceeding more than one person.

Upon the completion of the execution, a death certificate shall be issued by the State Medical Examiners’ Office with the time of recorded death, cause of death, and other necessary information prescribed in developed policy.
(a) The cause of death shall be listed as "lead poisoning," unless the execution is carried out by alternative means.
(b) The certificate shall be issued to the recipient and the Department of Justice in a timely manner.

The death certificate issued shall be enforceable upon signature by the Chief Medical Examiner, and cannot be challenged by the recipient alone without a legal petition to the Mayflower Supreme Court.
A person imposed with a judgment of death by a court of law may petition an appeal of their sentence to the Mayflower Supreme Court for a stay of execution.
(a) They shall be remanded in the custody of the Mayflower State Police until their hearing.
Any sentence of death upon acceptance of a Writ of Certiorari shall be stayed and paused until a decision by the Supreme Court is made in favor or against an appeal.
The Governor may grant a Stay of Execution to anyone whom is scheduled to be executed, indefinitely postponing their execution unless said stay is vacated by the Governor.
“Justified homicide” shall refer to the provisions as defined in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 7101.
“Trespassing” shall refer to the provisions as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3205.
“Attempting to trespass” shall refer to the attempt to commit a violation of 1 M.S.C § 3205.
“Trespassers” shall be defined as anyone actively trespassing or attempting to trespass.
“Unauthorized third party” shall refer to any person who is occupying or attempting to occupy private property without authorization.
“Innocent third party” shall refer to any person who is not in the commission of a crime.

“Identifiable public servant” shall refer to any person employed within the Mayflower National Guard, any Union of Columbia Law Enforcement Agency, Lee County Transportation Authority, or Lee County Regional Hospital who is acting in their official capacity, and is easily marked by a department or company uniform. Law enforcement officers who are in an unmarked capacity as defined by specific department policy shall be considered easily identifiable if they are wearing a badge of their respective agency on their person.
This chapter may be cited as "The Castle Doctrine Act."
A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest for using lethal, or any degree of force less-than-lethal, given it is a Justified Homicide.

A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest and is immune from civil claims for using less-than-lethal force if an unauthorized third party is actively trespassing or attempting to trespass and has been given ample warning(s) to leave and reasonable time to do so.
A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest and is immune from civil claims for using lethal or less-than-lethal force if an unauthorized third party is—
(a) has committed 1 M.S.C. § 3201 (Breaking and entering) and is actively trespassing on private property; or
(b) is actively attempting to commit breaking and entering.
A person is justified justified in, and cannot face prosecution nor arrest, and is immune from civil claims for using lethal force in defense of an innocent third party given:
(a) The innocent third party is actively being assaulted to a degree that would cause serious bodily injury or death.
(b) The innocent third party is actively being kidnapped.
(c) The innocent third party is actively a victim of armed robbery as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3101.
A person is justified in, and cannot face prosecution nor arrest, and is immune from civil claims for using less-than-lethal force in defense of an innocent third party given:
(a) The innocent third party is actively being assaulted to a degree that would not cause serious bodily injury or death.
(b) The innocent third party is actively being robbed as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3102.

records.text: When pursed through a criminal trial, the maximum incarceration time that can be awarded for a—
(a) Felony class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be eighteen (18) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.
(b) Misdemeanor class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be thirteen (13) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.
(c) Felony class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Vehicle Code shall be fifteen (15) times the length of its usual standard sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.
(d) Misdemeanor class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Vehicle Code shall be ten (10) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

No person shall be sentenced to a cumulative term of imprisonment exceeding one hundred twenty (120) hours for violations or enhancements imposed solely under this subchapter with respect to statutes designated as Active status, regardless of the number or combination of applicable enhancements. “Qualified immunity” means legal protection shielding a law enforcement officer from civil liability for actions performed in the line of duty, unless the officer’s conduct violates clearly established statutory or constitutional rights of which a reasonable person would have known.
A law enforcement officer shall not be held personally liable for civil damages for any act or omission arising out of the performance of their duties, if such act or omission—

records.text: Qualified immunity shall not apply where a law enforcement officer is found, by clear and convincing evidence, to have—
(a) acted with malicious intent to cause harm;
(b) engaged in conduct that shocks the conscience; or
(c) willfully violated state constitutional rights.
Qualified immunity shall not apply to actions taken by officers that are entirely unrelated to their duties, or while acting in a purely personal or private capacity.
Homicide by any person is justifiable when:
(a) committed in defense of an immediate threat to another person's life;
(b) committed by lawful means during the course of a peace officer's duties;
(c) committed by a peace officer lawfully engaged in protective duties of a public official;
(d) committed by an individual lawfully authorized by state statute to use deadly force; or
(e) committed with the consent of the victim for the purpose of resetting their character.

(i) However, a person/victim cannot consent to being killed under this clause if: (1) they are in the lawful custody of a peace officer, correctional officer, security officer, or any other person lawfully detaining, arresting, or holding them in custody; or (2) they are incapable of knowingly or lawfully giving consent.

For the purposes of this act, the term “euthanasia” or “euthanization” shall refer to the successful act of committing a homicide or otherwise causing the death of another person in a manner wholly compliant with subchapter (II) of this act.

The term “authorized healthcare provider” shall refer to any employee, agent, or assign of the Lee County Regional Hospital, a private healthcare contractor for Lee County, Mayflower, who has completed training and maintains a Paramedic certification, or the RHC540 certification course; or any employee, agent, or assign of the same who holds a doctorate degree in medicine from any accredited university within the Union of Columbia.

Any person who conducts a lawful euthanization under the complete compliance of the provisions of this act shall be free from criminal liability and prosecution for the actions taken to conduct that euthanization, including freedom from liability for the crimes of:

(a) Any crime that would otherwise have been considered to be committed under Title 1, Subtitle 2 of the Mayflower State Code, excepting crimes committed that were reasonably unnecessary or otherwise medically irrelevant to the euthanization process.

(b) Any crime that would otherwise have been considered to be committed under Title 1, Subtitle 7, Chapter I of the Mayflower State Code, excepting crimes committed that were reasonably unnecessary or otherwise medically irrelevant to the euthanization process.
Euthanasia shall be considered lawful when conducted by any individual who is not an authorized healthcare provider when:
(a) The euthanization is undertaken with the explicit, stated consent of the euthanized;
(b) The euthanized is not actively being pursued or remanded into the custody of a law enforcement agency;

(c) The euthanized individual is suffering from a debilitating physical condition that prevents them from experiencing an adequate quality of life, such as total loss of physical movement or total loss of access to game mechanics;
(d) The euthanization is executed with a legally owned firearm.

(e) The euthanization is executed at a reasonable distance away from other individuals and the general public from the site of euthanization and the path of travel for any projectiles discharged from the firearm, or executed at the site of private property where the euthanizer and euthanized have a legal right to access; and
(f) The euthanization is conducted swiftly and as painlessly as reasonably possible by discharging the firearm into the euthanized’s head.
Euthanasia shall be considered lawful when conducted by an individual who is an authorized healthcare provider when:
(a) They are actively working in employment, on shift, are compensated for, or are otherwise representing their healthcare provider at the time of euthanization;
(b) The euthanization is undertaken with the explicit, stated consent of the euthanized, or their legal guardian or next of kin if they are indefinitely incapacitated or otherwise unable to consent.
(c) The euthanized individual is suffering from a debilitating physical condition that prevents them from experiencing an adequate quality of life, diagnosed by an authorized healthcare provider;

(d) The healthcare provider has not coaxed, suggested, encouraged, influenced, or otherwise unethically persuaded the euthanized or their guardian or next of kin to consent to euthanization when they reasonably would not have otherwise without such guidance;
(e) Alternative medical treatment methods have been extensively exhausted with no improvement in physical condition;
(f) The euthanization is executed with a legally owned firearm, medically controlled lethal injection, or the intentional overdosing of a medication to hasten or cause death;

(g) The euthanization is executed in a controlled and private environment within a place of hospice care, and only necessary medical personnel and the euthanized person’s direct related family are present or in observance;
(h) Reasonable efforts have been taken to prevent the risk of injury or death to any party other than the euthanized; and

(i) The euthanization is conducted as swiftly and as painlessly as reasonably possible by discharging the firearm into the euthanized’s head or the effective monitoring of the euthanized’s physical condition throughout the entire process and the administration of medication or substances that would not be reasonably known to cause pain.

Any individual who conducts a euthanization and subsequently faces law enforcement investigation, detainment, subpoena or other search and seizure shall bear the burden of proof for statutory compliance, and such proof shall evidently show the entire euthanization process from start to finish and the actions taken to meet all statutory requirements to render the euthanization lawful; and that no negligence occurred to where any statutory condition becomes unsatisfied.

Any individual who fails to meet any statutory requirement stipulated by this act when conducting a euthanization, or otherwise conducts a euthanization under a provision that they do not otherwise meet the conditions and authorization for shall not be protected under section (a) of this subchapter and shall face full criminal liability for any conduct that would otherwise be considered a criminal action notwithstanding euthanasia.
An individual shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 2101 “First-degree murder” when they—
(a) Kill, or causes another individual to be killed, while in the commission or attempted commission of one of the following crimes:
(i) 1 M.S.C. § 1302 “Felony Misconduct."
(ii) 1 M.S.C. § 1308 “Felony Evasion."
(iii) 1 M.S.C. § 1311 “Escape."
(iv) 1 M.S.C. § 1312 “Obstruction of Justice."
(v) 1 M.S.C. § 4103 “Inciting a Riot."
(b) Kill, or causes another individual to be killed, while in commission or attempted commission of a felony under the following sections of Title 1 of the Mayflower State Code:
(i) Subtitle 1, Chapter I.
(ii) Subtitle 1, Chapter VI.
(iii) Subtitle 1, Chapter VIII.
(iv) Subtitle 2, Chapter II.
(v) Subtitle 3, Chapter I.
(vi) Subtitle 3, Chapter II.
(vii) Subtitle 4, Chapter III.
(viii) Subtitle 5 or 6.

(c) Are jointly engaged in the commission or attempted commission of any aforementioned felony, and does so with another individual who commits 1 M.S.C. § 2101 First-degree murder in the course of such a felony, and who thereafter continues to participate in any criminal conduct with that individual following the commission of said murder.
SHORT TITLE. This chapter may be cited as the "Federal Civil Rights Claims Enforcement Act."
DEFINITIONS. The term “Union” or “Union of Columbia” shall refer to the United States of America.

The term “federal civil rights law” shall refer to any law of the Union of Columbia codified in Title 42 of the Union of Columbia Code that protects individual rights against unlawful discrimination, official misconduct, or deprivation of rights under color of law, including but not limited to 42 U.S.C. §§ 1981, 1982, 1983, 1985, 1986 and related provisions.
“Person” shall include any natural person, corporation, partnership, association, union, or other legal entity, and where applicable, includes individuals acting under color of law.

The term “color of law” shall mean any act done by a government official, employee, or agent—whether lawful or unlawful—that is made possible by the authority or appearance of authority granted by law.
The term “court of competent jurisdiction” shall refer to any trial court of general or limited jurisdiction established by the laws of the State of Mayflower that is authorized to hear civil cases.

The term “state actor” shall include any official, employee, or agent of the State of Mayflower or any of its subdivisions, municipalities, or public institutions, as well as any person or entity acting jointly or in concert with such officials or institutions.

Pursuant to the sovereign legislative authority of the State of Mayflower and in accordance with Article One, Section Eleven of the Constitution thereof, the causes of action enumerated in subsection (b) of this Section are hereby adopted into law and may be enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction within the State of Mayflower.

records.text: In any action brought under this Act, the prevailing party shall be entitled to remedies, as applicable and consistent with the nature of the violation.

In cases where the defendant’s actions were willful, malicious, or reckless, the court may award punitive damages to punish the defendant and deter future violations. Such damages shall be determined based on the defendant’s conduct and the need to deter similar behavior in the future.
The court may issue an order for injunctive relief to prevent further harm, including but not limited to:
(a) Ordering the defendant to cease and desist from unlawful conduct;
(b) Requiring the defendant to take corrective actions, such as policy changes, training, or public notices;
(c) Mandating the defendant to take affirmative actions to rectify any wrongs or prevent recurrence.

The court may issue a declaratory judgment to determine the rights, duties, and obligations of the parties involved, particularly where there is uncertainty about the application of the law to the facts of the case.

The prevailing party shall be entitled to attorneys’ fees and litigation costs incurred in bringing or defending the action. The court may also award such fees and costs to the defendant if the court finds that the plaintiff's claim was frivolous or without merit.

Each day that a violation of this Act continues shall be considered a separate offense for purposes of calculating remedies, penalties, and enforcement actions. The court shall have discretion to impose additional penalties for each day a violation persists.

All remedies and penalties under this Section may be enforced by the courts of the State of Mayflower, including the issuance of orders of execution, garnishment, or other mechanisms as necessary to ensure compliance with any judgment, injunction, or restitution order.

The amount of punitive damages awarded in any case under this Act shall not exceed three (3) times the amount of compensatory damages, except where the defendant’s actions are determined to be particularly egregious or where statutory exceptions apply.

Any party who prevails in an action under this Act shall have the right to recover any penalties or damages awarded as part of the judgment, through any available lawful means of enforcement, including execution of judgment or garnishment.
It shall be unlawful for any person, entity, or government official to retaliate against any individual for exercising their rights under this Act, including but not limited to:

(a) Any individual who files or has filed a civil rights claim under this Act shall not be subject to retaliation, including threats, harassment, or adverse action taken against them in employment or in other aspects of their personal life.
(b) No person shall face retaliation for providing testimony, evidence, or assistance in any civil rights action brought under this Act, even if the action is ultimately dismissed or withdrawn.
(c) No person shall be retaliated against for opposing practices or policies that they reasonably believe to be discriminatory or violative of civil rights under this Act.
Retaliation under this Section includes, but is not limited to:
(a) Any adverse employment action, as stipulated under Title 4, Subtitle 7, Chapter 1, against an individual for exercising their rights under this Act.
(b) Physical or verbal harassment, threats of violence, or actions intended to intimidate or coerce an individual for asserting their civil rights.
(c) Refusal to provide goods, services, or benefits to an individual or group because they have exercised their civil rights or filed a claim.
(d) Any deliberate efforts to harm an individual's reputation, relationships, or social standing through wrongful means as a result of their involvement in civil rights litigation.
Any person who proves retaliation under this Section shall be entitled to the following remedies:
(a) As provided in paragraph 1601 of this chapter, compensatory damages for harm suffered as a result of retaliation, including but not limited to:
(i) Harm to reputation or social standing;
(ii) Loss of opportunities for advancement.
(b) As provided in paragraph 1602 of this chapter, the court may award punitive damages if the retaliation is found to be willful, malicious, or grossly negligent.
(c) The court may issue an order requiring the defendant to cease retaliation or restore the affected individual's rights or benefits.

(d) Where an individual's employment, services, or benefits were adversely affected by retaliation, the court may order the restoration of such rights or benefits, including re-employment or reinstatement to the same position.
(e) As provided in paragraph 1605 of this chapter, the prevailing party may be entitled to reimbursement for attorneys' fees and litigation costs incurred as a result of the retaliation claim.
In any action alleging retaliation, the plaintiff shall be required to demonstrate, by a preponderance of the evidence:
(a) That they engaged in a protected activity under this Act (such as filing a claim, testifying, or opposing discriminatory practices);
(b) That the defendant took an adverse action against them that would be considered retaliatory under this Section;
(c) That there is a causal connection between the protected activity and the adverse action taken.

Nothing in this Section shall be construed to waive any other legal remedies available to individuals under state law for retaliation, nor shall it limit any rights individuals may have to bring a separate cause of action under applicable laws for retaliatory conduct outside of the provisions of this Act.
